correctness.rationale: The invariant second-moment equation follows exactly by expanding the Gaussian Euler update. With Z=HV−Δ and Q=H²V−2HΔ+S, it yields the displayed two-defect formula; all denominators are positive because 0<H<2/λ. The independent-copy covariance identity proves Δ≥0 for radial nonincreasing h, and S>0 for nonconstant h by positive invariant density. Uniform Gaussian drift and minorization prove uniqueness and finite fourth moments. For hε=h0+ε exp(−kx²), convergence of invariant laws follows from uniform fourth-moment drift and uniqueness of the limiting Gaussian autoregression. The exact Gaussian covariance is negative with magnitude 2kV0²/(1+2kV0)^(3/2), giving the claimed sharp first-order sign reversal. The standalone code runs exact rational algebra and quadrature; those finite checks are not substituted for analytical proof.

Original full text of the motivating 2026 paper and relevant earlier 2024 primary paper were compared at matching equations and results. value.rationale: Mean physical time per gradient evaluation is the natural computational budget for an adaptive SDE integrator, and fixed-step comparison at the same invariant mean step avoids a misleading minimum-step advantage. The exact separation of a residence-time covariance defect from a squared-step dispersion defect is structural and predicts a sharp sign change at the Euler relaxation midpoint \(\lambda H=1\). An explicit smooth decreasing-tail policy makes the second-moment gap negative beyond the boundary, demonstrating that the safe-direction inequality is best possible. This identifies both a provable no-benefit domain and an overrelaxed regime where adaptation can help, without asserting any general trajectory or wall-clock advantage.
